entry.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01045-2 Researchers show that large language models cannot learn from spatial coordinates regardless of model or data scale. Specialized geometric neural networks consistently outperform language models for material property prediction.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #neuroscience

entry.title: Does a Flux-Defined Markov Blanket Screen Self-Replicating Gray--Scott Spots? A Computational Test of a Blanket Condition from the Free Energy Principle
entry.summary:
Friston's free energy principle holds that a system separated from its environment by a Markov blanket---a boundary whose states statistically screen its interior from its exterior---can be treated as performing approximate Bayesian inference, and that such blankets arise wherever coupling is short-range. We test this blanket condition in a concrete nonlinear pattern-forming system: self-replicating spots in a reaction-diffusion model that persist, compete, and reproduce. Directed boundary exchange and timescale separation hold up reasonably well, with qualifications.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #neuroscience #clean-tech
